post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Notificación instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). aggregation.description: Aggregation function. total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /SCHEDULE_DIARIO/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Schedule diario instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator

post.description: Performs a dynamic query on SCREEN_Y instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

field.description: Physical column name (required). aggregation.description: Aggregation function. filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /YSCRIPT_POSTBUILD/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - entity name or smartieId empty

get.summary: Get a page of a smartie (saved list configuration)
get.description:
Runs a saved list configuration (columns, filters, sorting) and returns one page of it.

**The keys of each `data` row are the smartie's configured columns, not the entity schema.** A smartie can include columns joined from related entities (aliased `<fkPrefix>_<ATTRIBUTE>`, e.g. `TIDD_NOMBRE`, `ALIV_PORCENTAJE`), which is why the response may contain fields that do not appear in this entity's own attributes. The `columns` array of the response always describes exactly what came back.

Columns whose attribute group the caller cannot see are dropped from both `data` and `columns`. If you need a stable, explicit column set, prefer `POST /TIPO_MATERIAL/query`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to 1 when omitted. A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

data.description: Rows of the page. Each row is keyed by the smartie's column names (related-entity columns included); `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. the query does not group or pivot).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

post.summary: Execute dynamic query without persisted smartie
post.description: Performs a dynamic query on Tipo de Artículo instances with custom columns, filters, sorting, aggregations, and configurable pagination. Use this endpoint for production-grade listings that require predictable performance, payload control, and advanced filtering. Unlike /search, /query allows explicit column selection and page size configuration, making it the preferred option for list screens, integrations, and high-volume data retrieval scenarios. This endpoint allows ad-hoc queries without requiring a saved smartie configuration.

requestBody.description: Dynamic query parameters including pagination, columns, filters, and search criteria

page.description: Page number (1-based). A page past the last one returns an empty `data` with the real `total` (iterate until `data` comes back empty, or use `total` / `pageSize`).

search.description: Free-text term applied over the requested columns: a LIKE '%term%' against each column in `columns` whose data type supports it, OR-ed together. It narrows both `data` and `total`. Combine it with `filters` for exact conditions.

field.description: Physical column name (required). Available columns from entity view, plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR) even though the resolved username (e.g. ORDC_SOLICITADA_POR_NOMBRE) is offered separately - request the raw id to cross-reference against your own user directory instead of the resolved display name. Same for the physical id of related entities (e.g. MATE_ID_MATE): request it to correlate each row with the related record in one call, instead of one filtered query per candidate.

aggregation.description: Aggregation function. As soon as one column has an aggregation, the query is grouped: every requested column WITHOUT an aggregation becomes part of the GROUP BY, and each row of `data` is one group (no `id`/`ESTA_CODIGO` keys); if every column is aggregated, the result is a single row. `total` then counts groups, not underlying records, and `page`/`pageSize` paginate groups. An aggregated column can be sorted with `sortDirection`/`sortOrder` (it orders by the aggregated value). `COUNT` counts DISTINCT non-null values of the column, not rows - to count records per group, COUNT a column that is unique per record (e.g. `id`). `filters` and `search` are applied to the individual records BEFORE grouping; there is no way to filter on an aggregated value (no HAVING). Any value outside this list is rejected with 400.

columns.description: Column specifications. If null or empty, default header columns will be used

columnName.description: Column name to filter (required). Same set as `columns`: entity view columns plus the raw id of Usuario-typed attributes and the physical id of related entities (e.g. CLIE_ID_CLIE). Attributes of a related entity are reachable only one hop away and only for the physical, non-relation attributes the view already joins (the `<ALIAS>_<ATTRIBUTE>` columns in this list); the related record's workflow state, its calculated attributes and anything two relations away are not filterable here - that needs a view entity that exposes it as its own column.

value.description: Value to compare. Type should match column data type

filters.description: Filter specifications. All filters are combined with AND; there is no OR between filters (for a set of values, issue one query per value or use `search`). Filters apply to the individual records, before any aggregation.

data.description: Rows of the page, keyed by the `field` of each requested column. `id` and `ESTA_CODIGO` are added when the rows represent instances (i.e. no column uses an aggregation).

total.description: Total number of rows matching the query, ignoring pagination. When the query aggregates (some column has an `aggregation`), each row is a group, so this counts groups, not the underlying records - and it is 1 when every column is aggregated.

columns.description: Definition of the columns actually returned - the authoritative list of the keys present in `data`

400.description: Bad request - invalid parameters, unknown column name, or unsupported operator
